purpose: Teach: 後遺症/火葬/引き起こさ/漏らし/退去/服従/脱退/揶揄

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、戦争被害者の後遺症を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: I see you wrote your paper on the long-term effects of war on survivors.
lines.style: Warm, measured confirmation. Slight pause before speaking, as if reviewing her notes. Gentle pitch. The tone of a teacher checking in, not testing.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、火葬文化の地域差を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I focused on regional differences in cremation practices.
lines.style: Quiet, precise. Brief hesitation at the start, as if still unsure he understood the question correctly. Steady voice, no defensiveness. The concentration of someone recalibrating.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、災害が引き起こさせた社会変動を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: So your research examined the social upheaval that disaster can trigger.
lines.style: Reflective, exploratory. Softer volume than before, like thinking aloud while speaking. A slight lilt at the end — genuinely asking for confirmation, not correcting.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、軍事機密を漏らした事件の歴史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Right — I actually examined the history of a military secrets leak incident.
lines.style: Careful, methodical. Small emphasis on the word 'actually,' showing he knows the topic shifted again. Patient tone. No irritation, just quiet accuracy.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 占領地からの住民退去を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: You've written about the displacement of residents from occupied territories.
lines.style: Engaged but thoughtful. A touch slower than conversational pace. The voice of someone genuinely trying to understand the thread of his research across topics.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、絶対服従を強いた組織の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — my paper traced how one organization enforced absolute obedience.
lines.style: Even-toned, unflinching. Direct but not defensive. A small breath before the summary, centering himself. Clinical precision without coldness.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、国連脱退の事例史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And your latest work covered the history of political satire cartoons during UN withdrawal.
lines.style: Warm, slightly wondering. A genuine pause before speaking, as if seeing the pattern across his work. Engaged but not performative. The voice of a teacher who sees something larger than the facts.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、揶揄的な政治風刺画の歴史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I looked at how mocking political satire and propaganda art documented that period.
lines.style: Firm, clear. A subtle emphasis mid-sentence on the historical scope. Exhausted but not defeated — the voice of someone who has explained his research many times and is still present for it.
